ui.sec.title: Who can do what, where
ui.sec.intro: This table describes the limits the controller actually applies when calling each CLI. Agents only work on a copy (worktree) of the repo; your source repo and machine are never written by agents directly.
ui.sec.how.read: Only inside the job's worktree. Claude/Gemini reviewers read a separate snapshot.
ui.sec.how.edit: Builders only, inside the worktree (Codex: workspace-write sandbox; Claude: acceptEdits). A read-only agent that changes the worktree blocks the job.
ui.sec.how.outside: The Codex sandbox blocks writes outside the worktree. Claude in -p mode denies anything not granted. Gemini headless blocks edits.
ui.sec.how.shell: Codex runs commands inside its sandbox (read-only when planning/reviewing). Claude builders run no commands; Claude reviewers only git status/diff/log/show. Tests are run by the controller from team.config.json.
ui.sec.how.network: Off by default for code work: Codex network_access=false with web_search off, Claude without WebFetch/WebSearch. Research jobs may search/read the web (disable with "researchWeb": false). Enable network per project with "network": true. The CLI itself still talks to its AI provider.
ui.sec.how.commit: Only the controller commits (checkpoints) to ai-team/<id>; blocked if an agent switches branch, rewrites history or leaves conflict markers.
ui.sec.how.merge: Only you, by approving. Fast-forward only, needs test + review + verify on the exact commit; high risk requires typing the commit.
ui.sec.how.push: The system never pushes or deploys. Agents are told not to push and get no production credentials; with network off Codex cannot push.
ui.sec.how.secrets: The controller removes *TOKEN*, *SECRET*, *PASSWORD*, *API_KEY*, AWS_*, AZURE_*, KINTONE_*… from the agent environment. Logs are redacted before saving.
ui.sec.how.accounts: Each member only uses its own sign-in profile (CODEX_HOME / CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR). Gemini Antigravity shares one Google session on the machine.
ui.sec.networkOff: agents have no internet (add "network": true in team.config.json to enable)
ui.sec.data1: Goals, guidance, and the code and diffs agents read are sent to that CLI's provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) for processing.
ui.sec.data2: Job history, messages and quota stay on your machine: .team/state/team.sqlite.
ui.sec.data3: The dashboard only listens on 127.0.0.1 and needs a local session cookie plus a CSRF header.
ui.sec.data4: Keep secret files (real .env, SSH keys, Kintone admin tokens…) out of the repo you give the team: agents can read everything in the worktree.
ui.sec.advice1: Run the whole system in WSL2 or a VM so Windows and personal files are out of the agents' reach.
ui.sec.advice2: Use only dev databases/tokens; deploy through CI with approval, never put production credentials on the agent machine.
ui.sec.advice3: Enable network for a project only when really needed (e.g. installing packages), then turn it off again.
srv.team.rigor_upgraded: The lead chose the light process but the job does not qualify (low risk, every task difficulty ≤ 2) → using the standard process.
srv.team.research_review: Check the research results: does each conclusion follow from the cited evidence, what is unsupported or missing? Return a verdict.
srv.team.strict_review: Strict process: review adversarially, look for every way this change could break.
srv.team.research_final: Write the final conclusion for the user: answer, reasoning, sources/evidence, confidence and open questions.

ui.mode.label: How to run
ui.mode.note: Automatic: short goals that avoid sensitive areas (auth, database, deletion, deploy…) go to one builder without the Manager; if it gets stuck or tests fail, it escalates to the Manager. Review/Verify only run when the risk gate asks.
